function.mechanism: Oxidation introduces carbonyl/carboxyl groups into starch polymers, altering viscosity, gel behavior, and processing stability.

adi.basis: EFSA (2017, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2017.4911) concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses and use levels for modified starches including E1404.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern for modified starches (including E1404) at reported uses/use levels; no numerical ADI needed.

adi.basis: ADI NOT SPECIFIED in oxidized starch/modifed starch evaluations; latest oxidized-starch entry includes 2018 specification-only review.

concerns.summary: Recent cohort studies on food additive mixtures (not E1404 alone) reported associations between some additive-mixture patterns including modified starches and higher type 2 diabetes incidence; causality was not established.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no genotoxic concern identified for the modified starch group including E1404.
EFSA 2017: no safety concern at reported uses/use levels; no numerical ADI required.
JECFA evaluations: ADI not specified for oxidized/modified starches.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI established by EFSA/JECFA for this additive group; EFSA reported high-percentile combined exposure for E1404-E1451 but still concluded no safety concern at reported use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current EFSA/JECFA conclusions and U.S. CFR authorization support low concern under authorized use conditions, while newer epidemiology raises non-specific mixture-level uncertainty rather than E1404-specific causal evidence.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 conclusion: no safety concern and no numerical ADI needed
JECFA ADI not specified with subsequent specification-focused updates
FDA authorization under 21 CFR 172.892 with explicit process/use limits
Recent concerns are mixture-based and not specific to E1404 alone
